programme.title: Cheers
programme.desc: Love Is a Really, Really Perfectly Okay Thing: Sam tells a lie, in an attempt to protect his friendship with Rebecca.

programme.desc: Snapped: Claire needs to clear the house before anyone makes her look bad in front of a reporter from an important women's business magazine. Jay invites Manny to a wine tasting.

programme.desc: Pool Party: Mitch and Cam help Lily overcome her insecurities about wearing a bathing suit to a pool party but discover that they have their own self-doubts.

programme.desc: Colombia v DR Congo (Kick-off 3.00am). Laura Woods presents all the action from both teams' second match in Group K, held at Guadalajara Stadium in Mexico. The Colombians have reached the knockout stage on three of the six occasions they have qualified for the finals, including their most recent appearance in 2018. Having faced Uzbekistan in their opening group contest, they will be looking to secure a place in the last 32 here before a final-game showdown with Portugal. However, they can take nothing for granted against the talented African outfit who are looking to make an impact in their first finals since 1974, when the country was known as Zaire. Colombia made a good start to their campaign on Wednesday with a 3-1 victory against Uzbekistan, while DR Congo played out an impressive 1-1 draw against Portugal. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Türkiye v USA (Kick-off 3.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group D match at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA. The USA have already won the group and will play in the last 32 on Wednesday in Santa Clara, while Türkiye have already been eliminated following defeats to Australia and Paraguay. Four of the five previous meetings between these nations have taken place since the turn of the century, and all of them have ended in a 2-1 scoreline. Two were in favour of the Americans, and the other two went the way of the Turkish, including the most recent encounter in June last year, when Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürko?lu were on the scoresheet in East Hartford, Connecticut. While the Crescent-Stars haven't appeared at a World Cup since 2002, the Americans had two group-stage matches against European opposition four years ago, beginning their campaign with a 1-1 draw against Wales that saw Gareth Bale equalise late on from the penalty spot after Timothy Weah had given USMNT the lead in the first half, before they moved on to play England in their second game, which ended in a drab 0-0 draw. With analysis from Juan Mata, Ange Postecoglu and Bradley Wright-Phillips, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon

programme.desc: Norway v France (Kick-off 8.00pm). All the action from the final match in Group I for both teams, held at Boston Stadium in the USA. This is the first meeting between the nations since 2014, when France prevailed 4-0 in a friendly. The French are likely to go into this fixture as favourites to win once again, but a closer contest is anticipated. Should they both be available, the game could see two of the world's leading forwards go head to head in Frenchman Kylian Mbappe and Norway's Erling Haaland, and it would be little surprise if either one of them proved to be the difference-maker this evening. The nations last met in the group stage of the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, when first-half goals by Pedro and Roberto Soldado gave the Spaniards a 2-1 win. That was a match between the reigning European and South American champions at the time, and coming into this encounter Spain are European champions once more after they won that title two years ago, while Uruguay were third in the most recent Copa America held in the United States in 2024. This is just the second-ever meeting between the two countries, with the first coming in the group stage of the 2018 World Cup in Russia. That game was a memorable one for the Three Lions as they brushed their opponents aside with a 6-1 victory. Braces from Harry Kane and John Stones, as well as a goal from Jesse Lingard, gave England a 5-0 lead at half-time before Kane completed his hat-trick in the second period. Panama did create some history in the second half as they scored their first-ever goal at the World Cup finals thanks to a consolation finish from Felipe Baloy. The Three Lions will be hoping to finish top of this group with victory here after they missed their chance to progress to the knock-out stages in their last game against Ghana, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by the African country. Four of the five previous meetings between these nations have taken place since the turn of the century, and all of them have ended in a 2-1 scoreline. programme.desc: Uruguay v Spain (Kick-off 1.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the third and final match in Group H for both teams, held at Guadalajara Stadium in Mexico. These two came into the tournament as the favourites to progress to the knockout rounds, but even if both teams' progression is already guaranteed, they will be eager to make a statement against strong opposition and look to top the group. The nations last met in the group stage of the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, when first-half goals by Pedro and Roberto Soldado gave the Spaniards a 2-1 win. That was a match between the reigning European and South American champions at the time, and coming into this encounter Spain are European champions once more after they won that title two years ago, while Uruguay were third in the most recent Copa America held in the United States in 2024. Spain picked up a much-needed win in their last game against Saudi Arabia thanks to a 4-0 victory, a result that puts them top of the table going into this match. programme.desc: Panama v England (Kick-off 10.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group L match at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA, as the two sides play their final group game. This is just the second-ever meeting between the two countries, with the first coming in the group stage of the 2018 World Cup in Russia. That game was a memorable one for the Three Lions as they brushed their opponents aside with a 6-1 victory. Braces from Harry Kane and John Stones, as well as a goal from Jesse Lingard, gave England a 5-0 lead at half-time before Kane completed his hat-trick in the second period. Panama did create some history in the second half as they scored their first-ever goal at the World Cup finals thanks to a consolation finish from Felipe Baloy. The Three Lions will be hoping to finish top of this group with victory here after they missed their chance to progress to the knock-out stages in their last game against Ghana, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by the African country. Panama are already out of the competition after two 1-0 defeats by Ghana and Croatia. With analysis from Roy Keane, Ian Wright and Gary Neville, pitchside inserts from Laura Woods, Emma Hayes and Karen Carney, commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon, and reports from Gabriel Clarke

The USA have already won the group and will play in the last 32 on Wednesday in Santa Clara, while Türkiye have already been eliminated following defeats to Australia and Paraguay. Four of the five previous meetings between these nations have taken place since the turn of the century, and all of them have ended in a 2-1 scoreline. Two were in favour of the Americans, and the other two went the way of the Turkish, including the most recent encounter in June last year, when Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürko?lu were on the scoresheet in East Hartford, Connecticut. While the Crescent-Stars haven't appeared at a World Cup since 2002, the Americans had two group-stage matches against European opposition four years ago, beginning their campaign with a 1-1 draw against Wales that saw Gareth Bale equalise late on from the penalty spot after Timothy Weah had given USMNT the lead in the first half, before they moved on to play England in their second game, which ended in a drab 0-0 draw. These two came into the tournament as the favourites to progress to the knockout rounds, but even if both teams' progression is already guaranteed, they will be eager to make a statement against strong opposition and look to top the group. The nations last met in the group stage of the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, when first-half goals by Pedro and Roberto Soldado gave the Spaniards a 2-1 win. That was a match between the reigning European and South American champions at the time, and coming into this encounter Spain are European champions once more after they won that title two years ago, while Uruguay were third in the most recent Copa America held in the United States in 2024. Spain picked up a much-needed win in their last game against Saudi Arabia thanks to a 4-0 victory, a result that puts them top of the table going into this match. programme.desc: Panama v England (Kick-off 10.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group L match at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA, as the two sides play their final group game. This is just the second-ever meeting between the two countries, with the first coming in the group stage of the 2018 World Cup in Russia. That game was a memorable one for the Three Lions as they brushed their opponents aside with a 6-1 victory. Braces from Harry Kane and John Stones, as well as a goal from Jesse Lingard, gave England a 5-0 lead at half-time before Kane completed his hat-trick in the second period. Panama did create some history in the second half as they scored their first-ever goal at the World Cup finals thanks to a consolation finish from Felipe Baloy. The Three Lions will be hoping to finish top of this group with victory here after they missed their chance to progress to the knock-out stages in their last game against Ghana, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by the African country. Panama are already out of the competition after two 1-0 defeats by Ghana and Croatia. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Türkiye v USA (Kick-off 3.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group D match at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA. The USA have already won the group and will play in the last 32 on Wednesday in Santa Clara, while Türkiye have already been eliminated following defeats to Australia and Paraguay. Four of the five previous meetings between these nations have taken place since the turn of the century, and all of them have ended in a 2-1 scoreline. Two were in favour of the Americans, and the other two went the way of the Turkish, including the most recent encounter in June last year, when Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürko?lu were on the scoresheet in East Hartford, Connecticut. While the Crescent-Stars haven't appeared at a World Cup since 2002, the Americans had two group-stage matches against European opposition four years ago, beginning their campaign with a 1-1 draw against Wales that saw Gareth Bale equalise late on from the penalty spot after Timothy Weah had given USMNT the lead in the first half, before they moved on to play England in their second game, which ended in a drab 0-0 draw. This is the first meeting between the nations since 2014, when France prevailed 4-0 in a friendly. The French are likely to go into this fixture as favourites to win once again, but a closer contest is anticipated. Should they both be available, the game could see two of the world's leading forwards go head to head in Frenchman Kylian Mbappe and Norway's Erling Haaland, and it would be little surprise if either one of them proved to be the difference-maker this evening. Both teams have already progressed to the knock-out stages after winning both of their opening games, and France will finish top of the group if they avoid defeat here

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Uruguay v Spain (Kick-off 1.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the third and final match in Group H for both teams, held at Guadalajara Stadium in Mexico. These two came into the tournament as the favourites to progress to the knockout rounds, but even if both teams' progression is already guaranteed, they will be eager to make a statement against strong opposition and look to top the group. The nations last met in the group stage of the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, when first-half goals by Pedro and Roberto Soldado gave the Spaniards a 2-1 win. That was a match between the reigning European and South American champions at the time, and coming into this encounter Spain are European champions once more after they won that title two years ago, while Uruguay were third in the most recent Copa America held in the United States in 2024. Spain picked up a much-needed win in their last game against Saudi Arabia thanks to a 4-0 victory, a result that puts them top of the table going into this match. programme.desc: Panama v England (Kick-off 10.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group L match at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA, as the two sides play their final group game. This is just the second-ever meeting between the two countries, with the first coming in the group stage of the 2018 World Cup in Russia. That game was a memorable one for the Three Lions as they brushed their opponents aside with a 6-1 victory. Braces from Harry Kane and John Stones, as well as a goal from Jesse Lingard, gave England a 5-0 lead at half-time before Kane completed his hat-trick in the second period. Panama did create some history in the second half as they scored their first-ever goal at the World Cup finals thanks to a consolation finish from Felipe Baloy. The Three Lions will be hoping to finish top of this group with victory here after they missed their chance to progress to the knock-out stages in their last game against Ghana, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by the African country. Panama are already out of the competition after two 1-0 defeats by Ghana and Croatia.
